_note: Hand-written reference summaries for the synthetic sample reports, used to compute ROUGE scores.
01_discharge_heart_attack.txt: 58 year old male with hypertension and uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus, a smoker, presented with severe chest pain, sweating and shortness of breath. ECG showed anterior wall ST elevation and troponin I was raised at 4.8 ng/mL. Diagnosed with acute anterior wall ST-elevation myocardial infarction, hypertension, uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus and dyslipidemia. Coronary angiography showed 95% occlusion of proximal LAD and primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug eluting stent was done. LVEF was 40%. HbA1c was 9.1% and LDL cholesterol 168 mg/dL. Discharged stable on aspirin, ticagrelor, atorvastatin, metoprolol, ramipril, metformin and pantoprazole. Advised to stop smoking and review in cardiology after 1 week.
02_discharge_pneumonia.txt: 67 year old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and COPD presented with fever, productive cough and breathlessness, with SpO2 88% on room air. Total leukocyte count was 16,400, CRP 96 mg/L and random blood sugar 312 mg/dL. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation with mild pleural effusion, and sputum grew Streptococcus pneumoniae. Diagnosed with community acquired pneumonia, acute exacerbation of COPD, poorly controlled diabetes and mild hyponatremia. Treated with oxygen, IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, nebulization, hydrocortisone and insulin. Fever settled by day 3 and she was discharged on day 6 on cefixime, inhalers, insulin glargine and metformin, with review after 1 week.
03_lab_report_blood.txt: Hemoglobin is low at 9.2 g/dL suggesting anemia, and ESR is raised at 34 mm/hr. Fasting blood sugar 132 mg/dL, post-prandial 205 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.4% are consistent with diabetes mellitus. Lipid profile shows dyslipidemia with total cholesterol 228 mg/dL, triglycerides 260 mg/dL, LDL 140 mg/dL and low HDL 36 mg/dL. SGPT 78 U/L and SGOT 52 U/L are mildly raised, possibly fatty liver. Uric acid is high at 8.1 mg/dL. TSH 6.8 mIU/L suggests subclinical hypothyroidism and vitamin D is deficient at 14 ng/mL. Kidney function is normal.
04_radiology_ct_abdomen.txt: A 7 mm calculus in the right distal ureter is causing obstruction with moderate right hydronephrosis and mild perinephric fat stranding. There is a 3 mm non-obstructing calculus in the lower pole of the left kidney. Other abdominal organs and the bladder are normal. Urology consultation is suggested.
05_discharge_dengue.txt: 22 year old male with 4 days of high fever, headache, body ache and vomiting was NS1 positive and diagnosed with dengue fever with thrombocytopenia, without warning signs. Platelet count was 48,000 on admission, fell to 32,000 and rose to 96,000 at discharge. WBC count was low at 2,900 and liver enzymes were raised. He was treated with IV fluids, paracetamol and ondansetron without platelet transfusion. Advised plenty of fluids, to avoid painkillers other than paracetamol, to return if bleeding occurs, and to repeat the platelet count after 2 days.
